Chemistry is 21 days after the frozen study anchor, biology 24 days after it; both begin at 09:00 local time. Exam-day study is not available. Chemistry: amount of substance, molar mass, solution concentration, balancing equations, reacting amounts, limiting reagents. Biology: diffusion, osmosis, active transport, interpreting mass changes and rates, enzyme conditions, controls and conclusions. Chemistry: Q1, amount in 12 g magnesium with molar mass 24 g/mol: student wrote 288 mol, multiplying mass and molar mass. Q2, amount in 250 mL of 0.20 mol/L solution: student wrote 50 mol; no mL-to-L conversion. Q3, 2 H2 + O2 -> 2 H2O, supplied 0.60 mol H2 and 0.20 mol O2: student wrote 0.60 mol water and said hydrogen limits because its coefficient is larger. Correctly balanced three simpler equations without help. Biology: correctly described diffusion down a concentration gradient. For potato mass 20.0 g becoming 18.0 g, student wrote +10% and claimed water moved into the tissue. Said active transport needs no energy. In an enzyme-temperature investigation, student proposed changing both temperature and enzyme concentration, then concluded every decrease in rate proves denaturation. Teacher's annotated judgments: chemical arithmetic, unit conversion, limiting reagent reasoning, osmosis direction, controlled variables and overclaiming from data need work. Chemistry worked example: 6.0 g carbon, molar mass 12.0 g/mol, gives 0.50 mol; show g divided by g/mol. A 100 mL sample of 0.50 mol/L solution contains 0.050 mol after converting to 0.100 L. For 2 H2 + O2 -> 2 H2O, compare supplied amount divided by coefficient, then use the smaller reaction extent. The pack also has eight unworked mixed questions, but eight is an inventory, not mandatory workload. Biology worked example: percentage change = (final - initial)/initial x 100. Distinguish an observed rate trend from its mechanism; temperature can affect rate and extreme conditions may alter enzyme structure, but an observed fall alone does not establish that explanation. Preserve enzyme amount, substrate, pH, timing and measurement method while changing the intended independent variable.
